description:
Alternative labels that `strip_catalogue_altlabels` must not remove, whatever their shape. The step removes supplier grades (`S 100`), trade names with a product number (`Garlon 480`) and database accessions (`NSC 147337`) by matching the shape of the string, because nothing in the Common Chemistry or ChEBI payload separates a catalogue entry from a name. A shape test cannot be right about every string, so this file is where a curator overrules it for a specific one.

Matching is on the label text, case- and whitespace-insensitively, after markup is stripped -- the same comparison the label pipeline uses everywhere else, so `PREFLUORO 116` and `Prefluoro 116` are one entry and not two. An entry applies to every flow carrying that label; the file does not key on a flow, because a name that is a name on one substance is a name on all of them.

`comment` is mandatory. Every entry asserts that a string which reads as a product code is in fact a name, and that assertion needs its reasoning attached -- what the string is, and where the claim comes from. An entry without a comment is ignored, which will look exactly like the entry not being there.

Whole families of designation belong in the code rather than here: refrigerant and halocarbon numbering (`HFC-134a`, `Halon 1211`, `Fluorocarbon 113`) and congener numbering (`PCB 118`) are already exempt by pattern, in `strip_catalogue_altlabels`. Add to this file when the string is a one-off; add to the patterns there when a source starts supplying a whole convention.

The list ships empty on purpose. When it was written, no string the filter removes was any flow object's preferred name -- so nothing was known to need overruling, and seeding it with plausible-looking guesses would assert what nobody had checked.
